statements.status_notes: The fix for CVE-2025-68161 was incomplete: it addressed hostname verification only when enabled via the log4j2.sslVerifyHostName system property, but not when configured through the verifyHostName attribute of the <Ssl> element. Although the verifyHostName configuration attribute was introduced in Log4j Core 2.12.0, it was silently ignored in all versions through 2.25.3, leaving TLS connections vulnerable to interception regardless of the configured value. A network-based attacker may be able to perform a man-in-the-middle attack when all of the following conditions are met: an SMTP, Socket, or Syslog appender is in use; TLS is configured via a nested <Ssl> element; and the attacker can present a certificate issued by a CA trusted by the appender's configured trust store, or by the default Java trust store if none is configured. This issue does not affect users of the HTTP appender. Users are advised to upgrade to Apache Log4j Core 2.25.4, which corrects this issue.
statements.impact_statement: Log4j Core ignored the verifyHostName attribute of a nested Ssl element, so TLS host name verification was skipped; fixed in 2.25.4. It matters only when an SMTP, Socket or Syslog appender is configured with a nested Ssl element and an attacker can present a certificate from a trusted CA. Docker images 5.0.0 through 5.0.3 have no standalone log4j-core. The Databricks JDBC driver inside liquibase-commercial-databricks.jar bundles a copy relocated to com.databricks.client.jdbc42.internal.apache.logging.log4j, whose class set matches 2.20.0, in range. Outside Log4j itself only the driver's bundled Netty logging adapter references it, and the jar carries no Log4j configuration file. From 5.1.0 that copy is gone, and log4j-core is bundled unrelocated in the liquibase-checks extension for the Phileas library: 2.25.3 in 5.1.0 and 5.1.1, in range, then the fixed 2.25.4 in 5.2.0 and 2.26.1 in 5.2.1 through 6.0.0. The build strips Phileas's log4j2.xml from that jar, so log4j-core runs with its built-in default configuration, which writes only to the console. The license-tracking application archived under /liquibase/dist carries only log4j-api with the log4j-to-slf4j bridge and logs through logback. No shipped jar contains a Log4j configuration that declares an SMTP, Socket or Syslog appender, and a source review found no Liquibase code that configures one.

statements.status_notes: Apache Log4j Core's Rfc5424Layout, in versions 2.21.0 through 2.25.3, is vulnerable to log injection via CRLF sequences due to undocumented renames of security-relevant configuration attributes. Two distinct issues affect users of stream-based syslog services who configure Rfc5424Layout directly: the newLineEscape attribute was silently renamed, causing newline escaping to stop working for users of TCP framing (RFC 6587), exposing them to CRLF injection in log output; and the useTlsMessageFormat attribute was silently renamed, causing users of TLS framing (RFC 5425) to be silently downgraded to unframed TCP (RFC 6587), without newline escaping. Users of the SyslogAppender are not affected, as its configuration attributes were not modified. Users are advised to upgrade to Apache Log4j Core 2.25.4, which corrects this issue.
statements.impact_statement: CRLF log injection in Log4j Core's Rfc5424Layout: the newLineEscape and useTlsMessageFormat attributes were silently renamed in 2.21.0, so newline escaping and TLS framing stopped working for a directly configured Rfc5424Layout; affects 2.21.0 through 2.25.3 and is fixed in 2.25.4. It matters only when a Log4j configuration declares Rfc5424Layout directly and sends it to a stream-based syslog service; SyslogAppender users are not affected. Docker images 5.0.0 through 5.0.3 have no standalone log4j-core. The Databricks JDBC driver inside liquibase-commercial-databricks.jar bundles a copy relocated to com.databricks.client.jdbc42.internal.apache.logging.log4j, whose class set matches 2.20.0, below the 2.21.0 rename that introduced the flaw, and the jar carries no Log4j configuration file. From 5.1.0 that copy is gone, and log4j-core is bundled unrelocated in the liquibase-checks extension for the Phileas library: 2.25.3 in 5.1.0 and 5.1.1, in range, then the fixed 2.25.4 in 5.2.0 and 2.26.1 in 5.2.1 through 6.0.0. The build strips Phileas's log4j2.xml, a single Console appender with a PatternLayout, from that jar, so log4j-core runs with its built-in default configuration, which writes only to the console. The license-tracking application archived under /liquibase/dist carries only log4j-api with the log4j-to-slf4j bridge and logs through logback. No shipped jar contains a Log4j configuration that declares Rfc5424Layout or a syslog appender, a source review found no programmatic Log4j configuration in this repository, and Liquibase's own logging does not use Log4j.

statements.status_notes: The Log4j1XmlLayout from the Apache Log4j 1-to-Log4j 2 bridge fails to escape characters forbidden by the XML 1.0 standard, producing malformed XML output. Conforming XML parsers are required to reject documents containing such characters with a fatal error, which may cause downstream log processing systems to drop or fail to index affected records. Two groups of users are affected: those using Log4j1XmlLayout directly in a Log4j Core 2 configuration file, and those using the Log4j 1 configuration compatibility layer with org.apache.log4j.xml.XMLLayout specified as the layout class.
statements.impact_statement: The flaw is in Log4j1XmlLayout, which ships in the Apache Log4j 1-to-Log4j 2 bridge (log4j-1.2-api), and in that bridge's Log4j 1 configuration compatibility layer when org.apache.log4j.xml.XMLLayout is configured. Both affected groups of users need the bridge on the classpath. No archive in the Liquibase Secure Docker images (5.0.0 through 6.0.0) contains the bridge or any org.apache.log4j package, including shaded or relocated copies. log4j-core is bundled only inside the liquibase-checks extension, at 2.25.3 in 5.1.0 and 5.1.1, 2.25.4 in 5.2.0, and 2.26.1 in 5.2.1, 5.2.2 and 6.0.0; the 5.0.x images do not bundle it there. The configuration bundled with the extension logs to the console with a PatternLayout. A source review found no reference to Log4j1XmlLayout, XMLLayout, or the Log4j 1 API. Releases from 5.2.0 onward are also at or past the 2.25.4 fix.

statements.status_notes: Apache Log4j Core's XmlLayout, in versions up to and including 2.25.3, fails to sanitize characters forbidden by the XML 1.0 specification producing invalid XML output whenever a log message or MDC value contains such characters. The impact depends on the StAX implementation in use. JRE built-in StAX: forbidden characters are silently written to the output, producing malformed XML. Conforming parsers must reject such documents with a fatal error, which may cause downstream log-processing systems to drop the affected records. Alternative StAX implementations (e.g., Woodstox, a transitive dependency of the Jackson XML Dataformat module): an exception is thrown during the logging call, and the log event is never delivered to its intended appender, only to Log4j's internal status logger. Users are advised to upgrade to Apache Log4j Core 2.25.4, which corrects this issue by sanitizing forbidden characters before XML output.
statements.impact_statement: Log4j Core's XmlLayout did not strip characters forbidden by XML 1.0, so a log message or MDC value containing one produced malformed XML or, with a strict StAX implementation such as Woodstox, an exception that dropped the event; affects every version up to 2.25.3 and is fixed in 2.25.4. It matters only when a Log4j configuration uses XmlLayout. Docker images 5.0.0 through 5.0.3 have no standalone log4j-core. The Databricks JDBC driver inside liquibase-commercial-databricks.jar bundles a copy relocated to com.databricks.client.jdbc42.internal.apache.logging.log4j, whose class set matches 2.20.0, in range, and the jar carries no Log4j configuration file. From 5.1.0 that copy is gone, and log4j-core is bundled unrelocated in the liquibase-checks extension for the Phileas library: 2.25.3 in 5.1.0 and 5.1.1, in range, then the fixed 2.25.4 in 5.2.0 and 2.26.1 in 5.2.1 through 6.0.0. The build strips Phileas's log4j2.xml, a single Console appender with a PatternLayout, from that jar, so log4j-core runs with its built-in default configuration, which writes only to the console. The license-tracking application archived under /liquibase/dist carries only log4j-api with the log4j-to-slf4j bridge and logs through logback. No shipped jar contains a Log4j configuration that declares XmlLayout, a source review found no programmatic Log4j configuration in this repository, and Liquibase's own logging does not use Log4j.
